target.title: fix(config): dedupe repeated validation warnings
target.body:
Related: #38295
Closes #25574

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running gateways can repeatedly log the same config-validation warning payload on every reload or write. Stale plugin entries are a common trigger, so service logs can fill with unchanged diagnostics that no longer add information.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config IO now fingerprints the sanitized warning payload per config path and emits it only when the payload changes. A successful clean full validation clears the fingerprint so a later recurrence remains visible.

The state machine deliberately preserves the prior fingerprint across transient invalid reads, skipped plugin validation, failed writes, and post-commit runtime-refresh rollback. Both load and write validation use the same owner.

This is a focused maintainer replay of the only unique remaining slice from #38295. Its broader restart/recovery work is already superseded by current `main`.

## User Impact

Operators still see each distinct config warning and any warning that returns after the config becomes clean, without repeated identical payloads filling logs during normal reload and write activity.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 411 focused config IO and gateway reload tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed`: scoped `core`, `coreTests`, and `docs` gate passed, including tsgo, changed-file lint, import-cycle, database-first, and boundary guards.
- Five skeptical autoreview passes drove the load/write/rollback state-machine coverage; final review was clean at confidence 0.91.
- `git diff --check` clean.

Contributor credit is preserved via the commit co-author and changelog thanks to @vincentkoc.
